newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES ROUT ROYALS IN IRABU RETURN TO MAJORS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES ROUT ROYALS IN IRABU RETURN TO MAJORS.

text.p: Japanese import Hideki Irabu
allowed three runs over 5 1/3 innings in his first start since
being recalled from the minors and Tino Martinez and Paul
O'Neill clubbed solo homers as the New York Yankees bounced
the Kansas City Royals 9-3 Wednesday.
Irabu (3-2), who made two starts at Triple-A Columbus
after he was shelled in consecutive starts with the Yankees,
gave up six hits, walked two and struck out five.
"I wasn't prepared enough the first time," Irabu said
through an interpreter. "The Yankees gave me an opportunity to
work on certain technical aspects, and that was the
difference.
"I wanted to get my velocity back on my fastball again and
the location of my fastballs. I learned to keep everything
simple and don't get overwhelmed."
The hard-throwing right-hander allowed a solo homer to
Chili Davis in the sixth and left the game two batters later.
All three of Irabu's wins have come at Yankee Stadium.
Ramiro Mendoza, Jeff Nelson and Greame Lloyd combined for
3 2/3 innings of scoreless relief for the Yankees, who have
won four of their last five games and 12 of 16.
Tim Belcher (11-11) allowed five runs and nine hits in 5
2/3 innings. He has lost consecutive starts and has given up
13 runs and 20 hits over 10 1/3 innings in that span.
The Royals have lost six of their last nine games.
The Yankees trimmed the Orioles' lead in the American
League East to 4 1/2 games.
In Baltimore, Andrew Lorraine outpitched Mike Mussina for
his first win in the major leagues and the Oakland Athletics
hit three homers in a 4-2 victory over the Orioles.
Lorraine teamed with five relievers on an eight-hitter. He
gave up two runs -- one earned -- in five innings, walking one
and striking out eight. Lorraine, a 25-year-old left-hander,
was brought up from Class AAA Edmonton.
Mark Bellhorn, Jason McDonald and Brent Mayne all homered
off Mussina (13-5), who had a personal three-game winning
streak snapped. In five innings -- his shortest outing since
Opening Day -- Mussina allowed four runs and seven hits.
In Chicago, Mike Cameron and Frank Thomas hit back-to-back
homers in a four-run fifth inning and Scott Eyre pitched five
innings for his first major-league victory as the White Sox
posted their fourth straight win, 5-2 over the Anaheim Angels.
Eyre (1-2), who had been pounded for nine runs over 9 1/3
innings in his first two major-league starts, allowed two runs
and six hits as Anaheim fell a half-game behind idle Seattle
in the A.L. West.
In Cleveland, the Indians and Tigers split a doubleheader.
Bob Higginson hit a pair of homers and drove in four runs
and Willie Blair (12-5) won for the eighth time in his last
nine starts as Detroit routed the Indians 13-3 in the opener.
Phil Nevin added a two-run homer and drove in three runs
while Damion Easley doubled, tripled and homered for Detroit.
The Indians salvaged the nightcap 9-1 as Orel Hershiser
made a successful return from the disabled list and Kevin
Seitzer and Sandy Alomar each drove in two runs.
Hershiser (10-5), activated before the second game,
allowed one run and five hits with two walks and two
strikeouts over 5 2/3 innings. He was placed on the disabled
list on July 29 with a lower back strain. Hershiser recorded
his 175th career victory and is 20-5 all-time at Jacobs Field.
Cleveland has a 2 1/2-game lead over the White Sox in the
A.L. Central.
In Boston, Juan Gonzalez homered twice for the fifth time
this season as the Texas Rangers took a six-run lead over the
first two innings and held on for their fourth straight
victory, 7-6 over the Red Sox, who lost their third straight.
Texas has won six of its last seven games, all on the
road. It went 6-0 in Fenway Park this year.
Gonzalez opened the scoring with an RBI single in the
first and extended the lead to 6-0 with a three-run shot off
Steve Avery (6-3) in the second. He capped Texas's scoring in
the fifth with his 28th homer.
In Toronto, Jose Cruz Jr's single with one out in the
bottom of the ninth scored Shannon Stewart, the new starting
center fielder after Tuesday's trade of Otis Nixon to the
Dodgers, as the Blue Jays edged the Minnesota Twins 3-2.
Joe Carter drove in the other two runs with his 200th
homer as a Blue Jay.
Stewart, whose ninth-inning single to left was his first
hit of the season, scored twice in the game.
Chuck Knoblauch homered and tripled for the Twins, who
have lost five straight.
Toronto shortstop Alex Gonzalez was hit on the hand by a
pitch from Latroy Hawkins in the third inning. X-rays revealed
a fractured right index finger.
